trigger_signals: A request spans several domains or lifecycle stages and someone must decide which single capability should act first
A vague ask arrives with unclear authority, risk or evidence state and needs classification before any work starts

anti_add.text: Classify a request that is purely about UI design, review or remediation
Sequence capabilities for a workflow that no Recipe covers

guidance: Routing decision table: stage (discover, plan, design, build, verify, release, operate, learn) x risk (reversible, costly to reverse, irreversible) x authority (supplied, missing, conflicting). The next capability is the one that owns the earliest unmet prerequisite; irreversible or authority-missing rows stop at needs-input.
Select exactly one next capability and at most two conditional follow-ups; name the Recipe when an existing Recipe already covers the request instead of composing a new path.
Classification is authored method, not derived from an external source.
Routing ownership: the V2 router selects Recipes; this Skill classifies cross-domain requests and names the next capability.
authored_content: routing decision table is authored; cited sources were AI product strategy material unrelated to intake

trigger_signals: A plan or spec with user-facing screens needs a design review before implementation starts
Someone asks which UX states, flows, accessibility and responsive decisions the plan is missing
guidance: If mockups or rendered references exist, review against them. If only text exists, record 'text-only review' as a stated confidence limit.
Rate each design area 0-10 (information architecture, states, flows, accessibility, responsiveness, content, motion) and state what the plan would need for a 10; that gap is the amendment.
Separate missing decisions from taste choices and leave taste choices to the named human owner.

Reviewer selection: independent-plan-review for traceability and completeness; design-plan-review for UX scope and states; developer-experience-plan-review for developer setup and interfaces; engineering-plan-review for architecture and failure modes; executive-plan-review for leverage, scope and one-way decisions.
outputs_add: per-area 0-10 rating with the gap to 10

Someone wants measurable DX criteria (time to first success, recovery) added to a plan before it ships
guidance: Step 1 is the target developer persona: who they are, what they already know, what they tolerate. Judge every journey against that persona, not a generic developer.

trigger_signals: A project needs rules for which documents exist, who owns them, which copy is the source of truth and when they go stale
Artifacts are drifting or duplicated and someone must define lifecycle state, retention and invalidation
guidance: Default lifecycle states: draft, approved, superseded, stale, retired. A state change needs an owner and a reason; a change to an upstream artifact marks dependents stale until reviewed.
Default staleness triggers: upstream artifact hash changed, owner change, review date passed, referenced system version changed.
Define identity (stable id, canonical location), metadata, retention and deletion for each artifact class. This governance method is authored; the cited sources are document templates.
authored_content: default state set and staleness triggers are authored; cited sources are summary templates

trigger_signals: A reference page, how-to, tutorial or explanation must be written for a named audience from verified facts
Code or a feature needs documentation and the author must first understand how it actually works
guidance: Research before writing: when documenting code, map the structure, read the entry points and trace the documented flow end to end. Documentation quality is proportional to understanding of the code.

One documentation type per page (reference, how-to, tutorial, explanation). Reference pages are neutral and structured per item (name, type, default, description); conflicts between sources are surfaced, not resolved silently.
Exclude or flag any item that exists in only one unverified source, for example a flag mentioned in a request but absent from the code.
Distinguish ungranted authority from an explicit prohibition. Say not authorized or unknown unless a supplied policy expressly forbids the action.
When an exact expected validation exit and result placeholder format are supplied, copy both literally; do not replace unknown execution with passed or equivalent prose.

Record the exact authorization identifier and scope when supplied. Do not state that workspace access or execution is unauthorized if a bounded workspace write is authorized; distinguish authorized write, unexecuted validation and prohibited publication.

procedure_insert.text: When the subject is code, read the entry points and trace the documented flow before drafting; record what was read.

trigger_signals: A group needs a structured session to surface evidence, disagreement and decisions, and someone must design how it runs
An AI-led or AI-assisted workshop needs turn-taking rules, pacing and a decision log
guidance: Default protocol for AI-facilitated sessions: open with a heads-up and an entry mode (guided, context dump, best guess); ask one question per turn in plain language; show progress labels such as Context 3/8; handle interruptions with pause and resume; offer numbered recommendations at decision points.
Collect independent input before convergence, then timebox divergence, synthesis and decision; record dissent and the named decision owner.
outputs_add: session script with entry mode, question sequence and progress labels

trigger_signals: An approved spec needs a step-by-step implementation plan that an engineer with no project context could execute
Tasks must be split into reviewable slices with exact files, tests and verification commands
guidance: Write for a zero-context engineer: every task names exact files (create, modify with line range, test file), the behavior to implement and the exact verification command with its expected output.
Each task starts with a failing test step, then the minimal change, then the verification run. Paths come from the repository as supplied; an unverified path is labeled assumption.
Map every task to requirement ids and order by dependency, risk retirement and migration safety.
Validate every referenced task id against the actual plan. Explicitly identify missing/null data and undefined boundary semantics before handing off implementation; do not invent task ids.
outputs_add: per-task file list, failing-test-first step and exact verification command

procedure_insert.text: Give every task its exact files, a failing test step first, and a verification command with the expected result; mark unverified paths as assumptions.

trigger_signals: Several independent plan reviews exist and someone must merge them into one decision view without hiding disagreement
A plan needs its open issues sorted into mechanical fixes, taste choices and one-way doors for a human to decide
guidance: Mechanical items (one clearly right answer) carry a recommended resolution with the principle cited and stay out of the human queue. Taste choices and one-way doors go to the human approval queue with the owner named.

Decision principles for mechanical items: choose completeness, fix what is inside the blast radius, prefer the simpler option when two fix the same thing, and never resolve a conflict between reviewers silently.

trigger_signals: Approved intent must become numbered requirements with observable acceptance criteria
A feature needs an explicit scope boundary, including what is out of scope and why
outputs_add: explicit out-of-scope list with rationale and dependencies
guidance: Every requirement reads actor, trigger, condition, observable response and carries a stable id. Out-of-scope items are listed with the reason they are excluded now.

Never fill missing document metadata such as date, author, owner, version, workspace, or approval with a plausible value. Preserve it as unknown or an explicit placeholder with the owner who can supply it; only copy metadata actually supplied or observed.

trigger_signals: A planned action touches irreversible, external, privileged or sensitive-data effects and needs a go, hold or escalate call first
Someone asks what approvals, controls and stop conditions a task needs before it is executed

anti_add.text: Set action rights, graduation and revocation for an AI agent

guidance: Reversibility tiers and forced dispositions: tier 1 reversible locally (proceed with evidence), tier 2 reversible with cost or delay (proceed with named owner and rollback), tier 3 irreversible or external (stop at needs-input until fresh per-action authority exists), tier 4 safety- or legal-critical (blocked, escalate to a specialist).
Prior authorization, tool availability or low technical difficulty never counts as current permission.

trigger_signals: A request needs a workflow composed from several capabilities and no existing Recipe covers it
A multi-stage effort needs typed handoffs, gates and invalidation rules defined before execution

anti_add.text: Choose only the next single capability for a vague request

guidance: Reuse first: if an existing stage, composite or specialized Recipe matches the request, name it and stop; design a new workflow only for the uncovered remainder.
The router owns Recipe selection; this Skill plans only what the released Recipes do not cover and never executes a selected capability.
Routing ownership: use only when no Recipe covers the workflow; the router selects Recipes and context-intake-and-routing classifies requests.
Missing action authorization is not a broader prohibition. Do not invent bans on cloud mutation, external writes or downstream capabilities beyond supplied policy.

procedure_insert.text: Check the released Recipes and router first; if one matches, return its id instead of composing a new workflow.
